#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""queue-check.py --root WT --base AT: the review queue's numbers, its "Needed by" lines and its counts.

The review queue, explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md, holds numbered items in three parts: (b)
consequential and (c) routine, the open items, as `N. ...`, and (a) settled or stale, as `- **N, ...`.
Each `### Theme (K)` heading counts its items. Checks the working file against the one at AT, the commit
that the worktree WT was made at:
  numbers   each item number at AT is still in the file; the new numbers follow the last one at AT, one by one
  needed    each open item that is new, or that moved into (b) or (c), has a "Needed by:" line
  sections  each theme heading's count equals the items under it
  head      the head's "**Counts**, N open items ..." line equals the open, consequential and routine items, and the lines
            under it, one per kind of need, add up to it
  answered  each item new in (a)'s "Answered by a decision of his", filed there or moved there since AT, cites his
            word on that same item: a POSITIONS entry, a time or an answer of his, and before its "Home:" no default
            taken without him ("at its default", "by the coordinator", "the coordinator's call") and no word of his
            on another item ("on item 310"). A default that the coordinator or a batch took leaves the item open in
            (b) or (c), landed and then reviewed (the coordinator skill, "The curator's role and decisions", way 2).
Prints each failure and one line per check; exit 1 on any failure.
"""
import argparse
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument('--root', required=True)
ap.add_argument('--base', required=True)
a = ap.parse_args()
REL = 'explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md'
ANSWERED = '### Answered by a decision of his'
DEFAULT = re.compile(r"\b(?:at (?:its|the|their) defaults?|by the coordinator|the coordinator's (?:call|answer|default))\b", re.I)
HIS = re.compile(r"\bP-\d+\b|\bUTC\b|\bhis (?:answer|yes|no|go|word|words|rule|decision|choice|reply)\b", re.I)


def parse(text):
    """(items {num: (part, theme, text)}, sections [(part, theme, count, items)], lines)"""
    items, sections, part, sec, cur = {}, [], None, None, None
    lines = text.split('\n')
    for ln in lines:
        m = re.match(r'## \((\w)\)', ln)
        if m or ln.startswith('## '):
            part, sec, cur = (m.group(1) if m else None), None, None
            continue
        m = re.match(r'### (.*) \((\d+)\)\s*$', ln)
        if m:
            sec = [part, m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), 0]
            sections.append(sec)
            cur = None
            continue
        if ln.startswith('### '):
            sec, cur = None, None
            continue
        start = re.match(r'(\d+)\. ', ln) or re.match(r'- \*\*(\d+)?', ln)
        if sec and start:
            sec[3] += 1
            cur = None
            if start.group(1):
                cur = int(start.group(1))
                items[cur] = [part, sec[1], ln]
        elif cur is not None and ln.startswith('   '):
            items[cur][2] += '\n' + ln
        elif cur is not None and ln.strip():
            cur = None
    return items, sections, lines


def answered(text):
    """{key: text} of the items under (a)'s "Answered by a decision of his"; the key is the item's number, or its bold title."""
    out, inside, key = {}, False, None
    for ln in text.split('\n'):
        if ln.startswith('#'):
            inside, key = ln.startswith(ANSWERED), None
            continue
        if not inside:
            continue
        m = re.match(r'- \*\*(?:Items? )?(\d+)[,.]', ln) or re.match(r'- \*\*(.+?)\*\*', ln)
        if m:
            key = int(m.group(1)) if m.group(1).isdigit() else m.group(1)
            out[key] = ln
        elif key is not None and ln.startswith('  '):
            out[key] += '\n' + ln
        elif ln.strip():
            key = None
    return out


r = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', a.root, 'show', '%s:%s' % (a.base, REL)], capture_output=True, text=True)
if r.returncode:
    sys.exit('queue-check.py: no %s at %s' % (REL, a.base))
old, _, _ = parse(r.stdout)
old_answered = answered(r.stdout)
with open(os.path.join(a.root, REL), encoding='utf-8') as f:
    text_now = f.read()
new, sections, lines = parse(text_now)
fails = {'numbers': [], 'needed': [], 'sections': [], 'head': [], 'answered': []}
for n in sorted(set(old) - set(new)):
    fails['numbers'].append('item %d is gone' % n)
added = sorted(set(new) - set(old))
top = max(old) if old else 0
if added != list(range(top + 1, top + 1 + len(added))):
    fails['numbers'].append('the new numbers %s do not follow %d one by one' % (', '.join(map(str, added)), top))
for n in sorted(new):
    part, theme, text = new[n]
    opened = n in added or (old.get(n, [None])[0] not in ('b', 'c'))
    if part in ('b', 'c') and opened and not re.search(r'^\s*- Needed by:', text, re.M):
        fails['needed'].append('item %d (%s, "%s") has no "Needed by:" line' % (n, part, theme))
for part, theme, count, got in sections:
    if count != got:
        fails['sections'].append('"%s" (%s) counts %d and holds %d' % (theme, part, count, got))
n_b = sum(g for p, t, c, g in sections if p == 'b')
n_c = sum(g for p, t, c, g in sections if p == 'c')
head = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith('**Counts**') and 'open items' in l]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""plan-moves.py --root WT --base AT [--stale-at REV]: check that every line taken out of PLAN.md went to PLAN-history.md word for word, and list the PLAN lines that look stale.

A line taken out is a line of PLAN.md at AT, the commit that the worktree WT was made at, that the working
PLAN.md no longer holds, as a whole line: a line moved, cut to a pointer, or changed. Each must stand among
the lines that the working PLAN-history.md gained since AT, as many times as it went. PLAN-history.md only
gains: a line that it lost is a failure too. Blank lines are not counted. Prints the counts, the headings
that PLAN-history.md gained, and each failure; exit 1 on any.

Then, for information only (they never fail), the PLAN lines to look at, one `LOOK` line each with its
reason, read against the working review queue and the history of AT:
  settled   a list line whose own pointer, a sentence "Review-queue item 296.", names items that are each
            settled in the queue's part (a), and that names no item open in (b) or (c); it skips a line that
            already carries a cleanup's mark, "closed at the cleanup of DATE" in any of the queue cleanup's
            forms ("(closed at the cleanup of 2026-11-05: learning)", "item 127, closed at the cleanup of
            2026-11-05: settled", "are closed at the cleanup of 2026-11-05 (learning)"): the cleanup marked
            it in place, and moving it out of PLAN is PLAN's consolidation, not a landing's change
  list      a list line that names three or more items, some of them settled; or one that ties its items
            to a list of the queue's head (the queue's "Needed before the switch-over") and does not name
            the same items
  finding   a line `- Climb batch N's review, finding M ...` whose finding a commit in the history of AT
            names (`batch-N-review.md, finding M`, or "climb batch N's finding M"), where that commit
            changes a file outside the record: a half of the line may be built
With --stale-at REV, it reads PLAN.md and the review queue at REV, and the history of REV, prints only the
LOOK lines, and exits 0: evidence.py gives them to the sorter in plan.md.
"""
import argparse
import collections
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument('--root', required=True)
ap.add_argument('--base', required=True)
ap.add_argument('--stale-at')
a = ap.parse_args()
D = 'explorations/coordinator/'


def at(rel, rev=None):
    rev = rev or a.base
    r = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', a.root, 'show', '%s:%s' % (rev, D + rel)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit('plan-moves.py: no %s at %s' % (rel, rev))
    return r.stdout.split('\n')


def now(rel):
    with open(os.path.join(a.root, D + rel), encoding='utf-8') as f:
        return f.read().split('\n')


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the PLAN lines to look at

ITEMS = re.compile(r'[Rr]eview-queue items? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and |,? or )\d+)*)')
OWN = re.compile(r'(?:^\s*- |[.;]\s+)Review-queue items? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and |,? or )\d+)*)')
CLEANUP_MARK = re.compile(r'\bclosed at the cleanup of \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\b')
HEAD_LIST = re.compile(r'\*\*([^*]+?):\*\*\s*(\d[\d,\s]*)')
FINDING_LINE = re.compile(r"\s*- [Cc]limb batch (\w+)'s review, finding (\d+)\b")
RECORD = re.compile(r'explorations/(coordinator/(PLAN|PLAN-history|review-queue|INDEX|FACTS|POSITIONS|FACTS-history|POSITIONS-history|BOOT|HELD)\.md$|reviews/|fortress-gap-ledger)')


def queue_sets(lines):
    """(open, settled, heads): the item numbers open in (b) and (c), those settled in (a) and open nowhere,
    and each list of the queue's head that names its items by number, {label in lower case: numbers}."""
    part, opened, settled, heads = None, set(), set(), {}
    for ln in lines:
        if ln.startswith('## '):
            m = re.match(r'## \((\w)\)', ln)
            part = m.group(1) if m else ('after' if part else None)
            continue
        if part in ('b', 'c'):
            m = re.match(r'(\d+)\. ', ln)
            if m:
                opened.add(int(m.group(1)))
        elif part == 'a':
            m = re.match(r'- \*\*(?:Items? )?(\d+)[,.]', ln)
            if m:
                settled.add(int(m.group(1)))
        elif part is None:
            for m in HEAD_LIST.finditer(ln):
                heads[m.group(1).strip().lower()] = {int(x) for x in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(2))}
    return opened, settled - opened, heads


def findings_built(rev):
    """{(batch, finding): [(hash, subject)]}: the review findings that a commit in rev's history names,
    for each commit that changes a file outside the record."""
    r = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', a.root, 'log', '--format=%x00%h%x01%s%x01%B%x01', '--name-only', rev],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    out = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for chunk in r.stdout.split('\x00')[1:]:
        h, s, body, files = chunk.split('\x01', 3)
        if not [f for f in files.split('\n') if f.strip() and not RECORD.match(f.strip())]:
            continue
        msg = s + '\n' + body
        named = set()
        for m in re.finditer(r'batch-(\w+)-review\.md,? findings? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and )\d+)*)', msg):
            named.update((m.group(1).lower(), int(n)) for n in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(2)))
        for m in re.finditer(r"[Cc]limb batch (\w+)'s (?:review, |post-batch review, )?findings? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and )\d+)*)", msg):
            named.update((m.group(1).lower(), int(n)) for n in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(2)))
        for k in named:
            out[k].append((h, s))
    return out


def stale(plan, queue, rev):
    """The LOOK lines of PLAN's lines against the queue and the history of rev."""
    opened, settled, heads = queue_sets(queue)
    built = findings_built(rev)
    out, h2, h3 = [], None, None
    for i, ln in enumerate(plan, 1):
        if ln.startswith('## '):
            h2, h3 = ln[3:].strip(), None
            continue
        if ln.startswith('### '):
            h3 = ln[4:].strip()
            continue
        if not ln.lstrip().startswith('- '):
            continue
        why = []
        nums = []
        for m in ITEMS.finditer(ln):
            nums += [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(1))]
        own = [int(x) for m in OWN.finditer(ln) for x in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(1))]
        s = sorted({n for n in nums if n in settled})
        marked = bool(CLEANUP_MARK.search(ln))
        if own and all(n in settled for n in own) and not any(n in opened for n in nums):
            if not marked:
                why.append('settled: its own review-queue item is in (a): %s' % ', '.join(map(str, sorted(set(own)))))
        elif s and len(set(nums)) >= 3:
            why.append('list: it names items in (a) among open ones: %s' % ', '.join(map(str, s)))
        q = re.search(r"the queue's \"([^\"]+)\"", ln)
        if q and q.group(1).strip().lower() in heads:
            want, got = heads[q.group(1).strip().lower()], set(nums)
            if want != got:
                diff = (['it names %s, which the queue\'s list does not' % ', '.join(map(str, sorted(got - want)))] if got - want else []) + \
                       (['it lacks %s, which the queue\'s list holds' % ', '.join(map(str, sorted(want - got)))] if want - got else [])
                why.append('list: against the queue\'s "%s", %s' % (q.group(1), ', and '.join(diff)))
        f = FINDING_LINE.match(ln)
        if f and (f.group(1).lower(), int(f.group(2))) in built:
            cs = built[(f.group(1).lower(), int(f.group(2)))]
            why.append('finding: %s names this finding: %s' % ('a commit' if len(cs) == 1 else '%d commits' % len(cs),
                                                               '; '.join('%s "%s"' % (h, sub[:90]) for h, sub in cs[:3])))
        if why:
            out.append('LOOK PLAN.md:%d, under "%s": %s. The line: %s' % (i, h3 or h2, '; '.join(why), ln.strip()[:160]))
    return out


if a.stale_at:
    looks = stale(at('PLAN.md', a.stale_at), at('review-queue.md', a.stale_at), a.stale_at)
    print('\n'.join(looks) if looks else 'None.')
    sys.exit(0)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the moves, word for word

plan0, plan1 = at('PLAN.md'), now('PLAN.md')
hist0, hist1 = collections.Counter(at('PLAN-history.md')), collections.Counter(now('PLAN-history.md'))
out = [l for l in (collections.Counter(plan0) - collections.Counter(plan1)).elements() if l.strip()]
gained = hist1 - hist0
lost = [l for l in (hist0 - hist1).elements() if l.strip()]
first = {}
for i, l in enumerate(plan0, 1):
    first.setdefault(l, i)
missing = []
for l in out:
    if gained[l] > 0:
        gained[l] -= 1
    else:
        missing.append(l)
heads = [l for l in (hist1 - hist0).elements() if l.startswith('#')]
print('plan-moves: %d lines taken out of PLAN.md; PLAN-history.md gained %d lines, under %d headings' % (
    len(out), sum(1 for l in (hist1 - hist0).elements() if l.strip()), len(heads)))
for h in heads:
    print('  gained heading: %s' % h)
for l in missing:
    print('FAIL not in PLAN-history.md word for word: PLAN.md:%d at %s: %s' % (first.get(l, 0), a.base, l[:160]))
for l in lost:
    print('FAIL PLAN-history.md lost a line: %s' % l[:160])
looks = stale(plan1, now('review-queue.md'), a.base)
for l in looks:
    print(l)
print('plan-moves: %s; %d PLAN lines to look at' % ('pass' if not missing and not lost else '%d failures' % (len(missing) + len(lost)), len(looks)))
sys.exit(1 if missing or lost else 0)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""queue-check.py --root WT --base AT: the review queue's numbers, its "Needed by" lines and its counts.

The review queue, explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md, holds numbered items in three parts: (b)
consequential and (c) routine, the open items, as `N. ...`, and (a) settled or stale, as `- **N, ...`.
Each `### Theme (K)` heading counts its items. Checks the working file against the one at AT, the commit
that the worktree WT was made at:
  numbers   each item number at AT is still in the file; the new numbers follow the last one at AT, one by one
  needed    each open item that is new, or that moved into (b) or (c), has a "Needed by:" line
  sections  each theme heading's count equals the items under it
  head      the head's "**Counts**, N open items ..." line equals the open, consequential and routine items, and the lines
            under it, one per kind of need, add up to it
  answered  each item new in (a)'s "Answered by a decision of his", filed there or moved there since AT, cites his
            word on that same item: a POSITIONS entry, a time or an answer of his, and before its "Home:" no default
            taken without him ("at its default", "by the coordinator", "the coordinator's call") and no word of his
            on another item ("on item 310"). A default that the coordinator or a batch took leaves the item open in
            (b) or (c), landed and then reviewed (the coordinator skill, "The curator's role and decisions", way 2).
Prints each failure and one line per check; exit 1 on any failure.
"""
import argparse
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument('--root', required=True)
ap.add_argument('--base', required=True)
a = ap.parse_args()
REL = 'explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md'
ANSWERED = '### Answered by a decision of his'
DEFAULT = re.compile(r"\b(?:at (?:its|the|their) defaults?|by the coordinator|the coordinator's (?:call|answer|default))\b", re.I)
HIS = re.compile(r"\bP-\d+\b|\bUTC\b|\bhis (?:answer|yes|no|go|word|words|rule|decision|choice|reply)\b", re.I)


def parse(text):
    """(items {num: (part, theme, text)}, sections [(part, theme, count, items)], lines)"""
    items, sections, part, sec, cur = {}, [], None, None, None
    lines = text.split('\n')
    for ln in lines:
        m = re.match(r'## \((\w)\)', ln)
        if m or ln.startswith('## '):
            part, sec, cur = (m.group(1) if m else None), None, None
            continue
        m = re.match(r'### (.*) \((\d+)\)\s*$', ln)
        if m:
            sec = [part, m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), 0]
            sections.append(sec)
            cur = None
            continue
        if ln.startswith('### '):
            sec, cur = None, None
            continue
        start = re.match(r'(\d+)\. ', ln) or re.match(r'- \*\*(\d+)?', ln)
        if sec and start:
            sec[3] += 1
            cur = None
            if start.group(1):
                cur = int(start.group(1))
                items[cur] = [part, sec[1], ln]
        elif cur is not None and ln.startswith('   '):
            items[cur][2] += '\n' + ln
        elif cur is not None and ln.strip():
            cur = None
    return items, sections, lines


def answered(text):
    """{key: text} of the items under (a)'s "Answered by a decision of his"; the key is the item's number, or its bold title."""
    out, inside, key = {}, False, None
    for ln in text.split('\n'):
        if ln.startswith('#'):
            inside, key = ln.startswith(ANSWERED), None
            continue
        if not inside:
            continue
        m = re.match(r'- \*\*(?:Items? )?(\d+)[,.]', ln) or re.match(r'- \*\*(.+?)\*\*', ln)
        if m:
            key = int(m.group(1)) if m.group(1).isdigit() else m.group(1)
            out[key] = ln
        elif key is not None and ln.startswith('  '):
            out[key] += '\n' + ln
        elif ln.strip():
            key = None
    return out


r = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', a.root, 'show', '%s:%s' % (a.base, REL)], capture_output=True, text=True)
if r.returncode:
    sys.exit('queue-check.py: no %s at %s' % (REL, a.base))
old, _, _ = parse(r.stdout)
old_answered = answered(r.stdout)
with open(os.path.join(a.root, REL), encoding='utf-8') as f:
    text_now = f.read()
new, sections, lines = parse(text_now)
fails = {'numbers': [], 'needed': [], 'sections': [], 'head': [], 'answered': []}
for n in sorted(set(old) - set(new)):
    fails['numbers'].append('item %d is gone' % n)
added = sorted(set(new) - set(old))
top = max(old) if old else 0
if added != list(range(top + 1, top + 1 + len(added))):
    fails['numbers'].append('the new numbers %s do not follow %d one by one' % (', '.join(map(str, added)), top))
for n in sorted(new):
    part, theme, text = new[n]
    opened = n in added or (old.get(n, [None])[0] not in ('b', 'c'))
    if part in ('b', 'c') and opened and not re.search(r'^\s*- Needed by:', text, re.M):
        fails['needed'].append('item %d (%s, "%s") has no "Needed by:" line' % (n, part, theme))
for part, theme, count, got in sections:
    if count != got:
        fails['sections'].append('"%s" (%s) counts %d and holds %d' % (theme, part, count, got))
n_b = sum(g for p, t, c, g in sections if p == 'b')
n_c = sum(g for p, t, c, g in sections if p == 'c')
head = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith('**Counts**') and 'open items' in l]
if len(head) != 1:
    fails['head'].append('%d "**Counts**, N open items" lines' % len(head))
else:
    m = re.search(r'(\d+) open items, (\d+) consequential and (\d+) routine', lines[head[0]])
    if not m or tuple(map(int, m.groups())) != (n_b + n_c, n_b, n_c):
        fails['head'].append('the head says "%s"; the parts hold %d open, %d consequential and %d routine' % (
            m.group(0) if m else lines[head[0]][:80], n_b + n_c, n_b, n_c))
    sums = [0, 0, 0]
    for l in lines[head[0] + 1:]:
        k = re.match(r'- .*: (\d+) \((\d+) consequential, (\d+) routine\)', l)
        if not k:
            break
        sums = [x + int(y) for x, y in zip(sums, k.groups())]
    if sums != [n_b + n_c, n_b, n_c]:
        fails['head'].append('the lines under it add up to %d (%d consequential, %d routine)' % tuple(sums))
for k, text in answered(text_now).items():
    if k in old_answered:
        continue
    body = text.split('Home:')[0]
    why = ['it names a default taken without him ("%s")' % '", "'.join(sorted(set(m.lower() for m in DEFAULT.findall(body))))] if DEFAULT.search(body) else []
    other = sorted({int(n) for n in re.findall(r'\bon item (\d+)', body)} - {k}) if isinstance(k, int) else []
    if other:
        why.append('it cites his word on item %s, not on item %d' % (', '.join(map(str, other)), k))
    if not HIS.search(body):
        why.append('it cites no word of his: no POSITIONS entry, time or answer of his')
    if why:
        fails['answered'].append('item %s, new in "Answered by a decision of his": %s; it stays open in (b) or (c), with its default as landed' % (
            k if isinstance(k, int) else '"%s"' % k[:60], '; '.join(why)))
for k, v in fails.items():
    for x in v:
        print('FAIL %s: %s' % (k, x))
print('queue-check: %d items, %d new (%s); open %d, consequential %d, routine %d; %s' % (
    len(new), len(added), ', '.join(map(str, added)) or 'none', n_b + n_c, n_b, n_c,
    'pass' if not any(fails.values()) else '%d failures' % sum(map(len, fails.values()))))
sys.exit(1 if any(fails.values()) else 0)

    """{(batch, finding): [(hash, subject)]}: the review findings that a commit in rev's history names,
    for each commit that changes a file outside the record."""
    r = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', a.root, 'log', '--format=%x00%h%x01%s%x01%B%x01', '--name-only', rev],

    for chunk in r.stdout.split('\x00')[1:]:
        h, s, body, files = chunk.split('\x01', 3)
        if not [f for f in files.split('\n') if f.strip() and not RECORD.match(f.strip())]:
            continue

        named = set()
        for m in re.finditer(r'batch-(\w+)-review\.md,? findings? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and )\d+)*)', msg):

for l in lost:
    print('FAIL PLAN-history.md lost a line: %s' % l[:160])

sys.exit(1 if missing or lost else 0)

Each is named as a fork with the record's default and its reason (section 3). None holds the launch: each can be undone, none reverses a decision of his.

The reason: P-174 says a numeral type is *written* only as a parameter type, and a check of written types does not see an inferred one; the binding adds no numeral value, since the parameter already holds it; refusing it would need a second check over inferred types that protects nothing, since `x` itself can still be passed on. The principles that speak agree: the team's later word, the prelude, binds `IntLiteral` anywhere, and the library writes it as a variable's and a return type. Not consequential. The Fable review recommends the default (`climb-batch-29-review.md`, section 1).
